title: Stamp duty on residential property transfers (South Australia)
summary: South Australia charges transfer (stamp) duty on purchases of homes and residential land under the Stamp Duties Act 1923 (SA), at rates that rise with the price. Buyers pay it up front each time a property changes hands.

instruments.title: Stamp Duties Act 1923 (SA)
instruments.provisions: duty on transfers of residential land

direction_rationale: Duty on every purchase raises the cost of moving, so households move less often, including to take better jobs, and homes are less well matched to the people in them. Treasury estimates each extra dollar raised by conveyancing duty costs 72 cents in lost efficiency, among the highest of the taxes it studied.

assessment.summary: A tax on buying a home, paid every time property changes hands. It discourages people from moving, including for work, and is one of the least efficient taxes in Australia; a broad annual land tax raising the same revenue would cost far less.

marks.reason: A transaction tax in the largest asset market, with an efficiency cost Treasury puts at 72 cents per extra dollar raised.
Raises the cost of moving home, so fewer people move to take better jobs.
